react.note: React itself: components, props, state and hooks

react-native.note: The framework: turns React components into real iOS/Android views

@react-native/new-app-screen.note: The template's welcome screen; remove it when you build your own UI

@react-navigation/native.note: Core of React Navigation: NavigationContainer and navigation hooks

@react-navigation/native-stack.note: Stack navigator using native screens (push/pop with a back button)

@react-navigation/stack.note: Stack navigator written in JavaScript (more customizable animations)

@react-navigation/bottom-tabs.note: Tab bar at the bottom of the screen

@react-navigation/drawer.note: Side menu that slides in from the edge

@react-navigation/elements.note: Shared UI pieces (headers, buttons) used by React Navigation

react-native-screens.note: Native screen containers; makes navigation faster (needed by React Navigation)

react-native-safe-area-context.note: Keeps content away from the notch, status bar and home bar

react-native-vector-icons.note: Icon fonts (Ionicons, MaterialIcons, ...); older all-in-one package

nativewind.note: Style components with Tailwind CSS class names

react-native-reanimated.note: Smooth animations that run on the UI thread

react-native-worklets.note: Runs small JS functions on other threads (used by Reanimated)

react-native-gesture-handler.note: Native touch gestures: swipe, pan, pinch (used by drawers and sheets)

zustand.note: Small, simple global state (share data between screens)

@reduxjs/toolkit.note: Redux with less boilerplate: global state with slices

react-redux.note: Connects Redux state to React components

jotai.note: Global state built from small pieces called atoms

@tanstack/react-query.note: Fetches, caches and refreshes server data (loading/error states for you)

axios.note: HTTP client; an alternative to the built-in fetch()

react-hook-form.note: Form state and validation without lots of re-renders

zod.note: Describe the shape of data and validate it (forms, API responses)

@react-native-async-storage/async-storag.note: Save small key-value data on the device (not encrypted)

react-native-mmkv.note: Very fast key-value storage on the device

react-native-keychain.note: Store secrets (tokens, passwords) in the secure Keychain/Keystore

react-native-permissions.note: Ask for and check permissions (camera, location, ...)

react-native-device-info.note: Info about the device: model, OS version, app version

react-native-config.note: Read values from .env files in JS and native code

@babel/core.note: Babel compiler; Metro uses it to transform your code

@babel/preset-env.note: Babel settings for modern JavaScript syntax

@babel/runtime.note: Helper functions Babel adds to compiled code

@react-native/babel-preset.note: Babel settings that turn TypeScript/JSX into JavaScript for Metro

@react-native/metro-config.note: Default settings for Metro, the bundler that `npm start` runs

@react-native/typescript-config.note: Shared tsconfig settings for React Native projects

typescript.note: TypeScript compiler; `npx tsc` checks your types

@react-native-community/cli.note: The `react-native` command: start, run-android, run-ios, doctor

@react-native-community/cli-platform-*.note: Adds {rest} commands to the CLI (`npm run {rest}`)

@react-native/jest-preset.note: Jest settings that mock native code so tests run on your computer

react-test-renderer.note: Renders components in tests without a phone or simulator

@testing-library/react-native.note: Test components the way a user uses them (press, type, find text)

eslint.note: Finds problems in your code (`npm run lint`)

files.App.tsx: Root component: the first screen of your app is rendered from here
files.App.js: Root component: the first screen of your app is rendered from here
files.index.js: Entry point: registers App with AppRegistry so native code can start it
files.app.json: App name and display name used by the native projects
files.package.json: Lists your JS packages and npm scripts (npm start, npm run ios, ...)
files.package-lock.json: Exact versions npm installed; commit it so `npm ci` installs the same
files.yarn.lock: Exact versions Yarn installed; commit it (use only one package manager)
files.pnpm-lock.yaml: Exact versions pnpm installed; commit it (use only one package manager)
files.bun.lock: Exact versions Bun installed; commit it (use only one package manager)
files.node_modules: Installed JS packages for this project only; not committed, `npm ci` recreates it
files.android: Native Android project (Gradle); open this folder in Android Studio
files.ios: Native iOS project (Xcode + CocoaPods); open the .xcworkspace in Xcode
files.src: Your app code: screens, components, hooks, ...
files.babel.config.js: Babel settings: how your code is transformed before bundling
files.metro.config.js: Metro settings: the bundler that serves your JS to the app
files..watchmanconfig: Settings for Watchman, the file watcher Metro uses
files.Gemfile: Ruby gems for this project, mainly the CocoaPods version iOS needs
files.Gemfile.lock: Exact Ruby gem versions; commit it
files..bundle: Bundler settings (installs gems into vendor/ for this project only)
files.vendor: Ruby gems installed by `bundle install` for this project only
files..nvmrc: Node version for this project; `nvm use` reads it
files..node-version: Node version for this project (read by fnm, Volta, nodenv, ...)
files..java-version: Java (JDK) version for this project, read by jenv or a shell hook
files..ruby-version: Ruby version for this project, read by rbenv/rvm
files..gitignore: Files git should not track (node_modules, build output, ...)
files..env: Environment values like API URLs; usually not committed
files.README.md: Notes about the project for you and your teammates
files..vscode: VS Code settings for this project
